author: director-TIG
message:
VOID-022 fix: busy-CAD backoff — heartbeat starved buyer RX of invoices

Bench finding: a due heartbeat re-scanned CAD every loop iteration
while the channel was busy. Each scanChannel pulls the SX1262 out of
RX mode, so the buyer could DETECT the seller's re-advertised invoices
but never sat in RX long enough to RECEIVE one — wedged at "DELIVERY
RECEIVED" with heartbeats still flowing.

- heartbeat_tx: 1 s backoff after a busy CAD (droppable telemetry,
  never tight-loops); inputs gathered before the scan; TX aborted if a
  frame lands mid-CAD (shared FIFO base — never clobber a reception);
  "HB: channel busy - deferred" breadcrumb.
- seller/buyer: lost-wakeup recovery — synthesise rx_flag if RxDone is
  latched with no DIO1 edge seen (250 ms poll), so a frame can never
  rot unnoticed in the FIFO.
- bouncer: echo unmatched buyer-serial lines as [SAT-B] — the buyer's
  diagnostics were invisible (its USB serial is owned by the bouncer),
  which made this wedge needlessly hard to triage.

pio seller_alpha + buyer_alpha SUCCESS (CERT -Werror); ground_station
rebuilt clean; ctest green. RadioLib internals verified sound
(startReceive clears IRQ + remaps DIO1) — the bug was ours.

author: director-TIG
message:
VOID-139: fix PacketA CRC-fail (phantom RX) + restore D-leg; flat-sat hardening

Root cause of the recurring "PacketA CRC fail" on the buyer was NOT RF
collision but a phantom RX after every transmit. setDio1Action(onRxDone)
maps DIO1 to fire on TxDone AND CadDone as well as RxDone, and RadioLib
never detaches the ISR during the blocking transmit(). So every buyer
relay (PacketB / ACK / PacketC) and every CAD scan set rx_flag=true; the
next loop read the STALE last-RX length (80 = SIZE_PACKET_A) via
getPacketLength() and pulled the just-transmitted FIFO bytes (TX/RX share
base 0x00). Those bytes carry APID 100 (shared by PacketA and PacketC),
so they entered the PacketA branch and failed the app-layer CRC. Since
LoRa PHY CRC is on (SX126x begin() -> setCRC(2)), a genuinely corrupted
frame is dropped at readData() with ERR_CRC_MISMATCH and never reaches
that check — proving the bytes were clean-but-wrong, not corrupted.

Fixes:
- void_protocol: add isRealReception() — gate on RADIOLIB_SX126X_IRQ_RX_DONE
  via getIrqFlags(); buyer.cpp + seller.cpp reject the phantom before
  touching getPacketLength()/readData().
- seller getAPID(): make tier-aware (SNLP APID at buf[4]/buf[5] under
  VOID_PROTOCOL_TYPE==2). It was reading CCSDS offsets, so inbound SNLP
  PacketC never matched SELLER_APID and PacketD was never emitted — this
  restores the long-missing D-leg.

Also in this flat-sat hardening pass (VOID-139):
- ground-station serial_hal: std::mutex around all serial writes (3 threads
  were racing PACKET_C_TX/PACKET_ACK_TX/CLI lines).
- gateway: anchor receipts.json to repo root via .git walk-up (fail loud),
  killing the CWD-relative nested gateway/gateway/data/ split; explicit
  VOID_RECEIPTS_PATH still wins.
- firmware: seller ADVERTISING/AWAITING_RECEIPT beacon state machine +
  light SX1262 CAD listen-before-talk (channelClear/transmitWhenClear).
  These targeted the earlier collision theory; kept as hygiene for the
  shared half-duplex channel (keep/revert TBD next session).

Verification: both seller_alpha + buyer_alpha compile SUCCESS under full
CERT -Werror flags; gateway go build + go test all pass; ground-station
41/41 ctest green. Bench-confirmed this session: seller now delivers
PacketD. NOT yet done: visible loop close (seller "UNLOCKED" indicator +

message:
gateway: migrate ingest + tests to regenerated protocol package

The kaitai-generated parser was regenerated from the modular KSY tree
at docs/kaitai_struct/ into a new gateway/internal/void_protocol/protocol
sub-package. This commit migrates every consumer to the new package and
removes the obsolete monolithic generated file.

  - Header types moved out of root: VoidProtocol_HeaderSnlp -> SnlpHeader,
    VoidProtocol_HeaderCcsds -> CcsdsPrimaryHeader.

    variants per F-04 fixed-tunnel-size rule. The ingest type-switch

    the old runtime length check is now redundant.

- they hold the wire-format invariants (PacketBBodyLen=178,
PacketBSigScopeBody=106, SNLPHeaderLen=14, ValidateFrameCRC32) that the

Fix KSY body bugs + promote hardened schema as source of truth (#6)

* VOID-006 F-03: magic-byte discriminant at body offset 0

Closes the dispatch_122 single-bit-flip collision between Packet D
(0xD0) and Packet ACK SNLP (0xAC). The 1-byte magic is absorbed
from the existing head pad on both packets, so frame totals and
every %4/%8 alignment static_assert are unchanged. Hamming
distance 4 guarantees a single RF bit-flip cannot cross types.

Enforced at three layers:
- KSY: dispatch_122 routes on a peeked magic byte; both ACK body
  variants and packet_d_body carry a contents-locked magic field.
- C++: PacketD_t / PacketAck_t (CCSDS + SNLP) gain a magic field
  with offsetof-based static_asserts proving downstream fields
  have not drifted.
- Gateway: ingest handler performs application-layer magic-byte
  verification before trusting the Kaitai dispatch, rejecting any
  mismatch with HTTP 400.

Also rolled in: BUG-1 (illegal doc: inside asset_id enum), F-01
(SNLP header locked to 14B with unified body_length formula),
F-04 (packet_ack_body split into tier-distinct CCSDS/SNLP types).
Golden vectors for packet_d and packet_ack regenerated under
both tiers; regression suites updated to assert magic presence.

message:
VOID-110/111/112/113/114B: nonce, sig scope, bounds, headers, alignment (#1)

* VOID-110/111/112/113/114B: fix nonce, sig scope, bounds, headers, alignment

Landmark change covering five audit-driven tickets:

- VOID-110: Remove 4-byte wire nonce from Packet B. ChaCha20 nonce is
  now derived deterministically as sat_id[4] || epoch_ts[8] (both LE).
  Monotonic-epoch guardrails persist last_tx_epoch_ms to NVS and gate
  TX on GPS-fix. Makes nonce reuse physically impossible.

- VOID-111: Signature scope is now identical across CCSDS and SNLP.
  The signer uses offsetof(PacketB_t, signature) so it adapts to any
  body reshape automatically. Covers header + body[0..105] = 106 body
  bytes through end of _pre_sig under both tiers.

- VOID-112: Packet B ingest handler validates packetSize >= 178 before
  any struct cast, rejecting short frames with 400.

- VOID-113: SNLP header locked at 14 bytes (sync_word[4] + ccsds[6] +
  align_pad[4]). 14 is the only size that maintains 6 (mod 8)
  congruence with the CCSDS header, which is the necessary condition
  for both tiers to share a single body layout. See
  docs/VOID_114_SNLP_HEADER_ALIGNMENT_DECISION_2026-04-14.md.

- VOID-114B: Per-field natural alignment for Packets A, B, L under
  both tiers, plus frame-total 8-byte alignment across every packet
  type for DMA-coalesced SPI bursts to the SX1262 on ESP32-S3 /
  Heltec LoRa V3 hardware. See
  docs/VOID_114B_BODY_ALIGNMENT_2026-04-14.md.

Frame sizes (all divisible by 8):

  Packet      CCSDS   SNLP
  A Invoice    72      80
  B Payment   184     192  (3x64, cache-line clean)
  C Receipt   104     112
  D Delivery  128     136
  H Handshake 112     120
  ACK         120     136
  L Heartbeat  40      48

Touched: void_packets.h, void_packets_ccsds.h, void_packets_snlp.h,
security_manager.{h,cpp}, void_protocol_final_v2.ksy,
gateway/internal/void_protocol/void_protocol.go,
gateway/test/utils/generate_packets.go,
gateway/internal/api/handlers/ingest.go,
docs/Protocol-spec-CCSDS.md, docs/Protocol-spec-SNLP.md, plus four
new decision/audit docs under docs/.

Verified: go build ./... clean; generate_packets.go emits A=72/80,
B=184/192, L=40/48, all other packet sizes unchanged.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* VOID-114B: enforce 32/64-bit packet alignment via static_asserts

Add compile-time guards on every packet type asserting both:
  sizeof(X) % 4 == 0   // 32-bit machine cycle aligned
  sizeof(X) % 8 == 0   // 64-bit machine cycle aligned

This locks the VOID-114B frame-total alignment invariant into the
firmware build itself — any future packet edit that breaks ÷8
alignment fails to compile rather than failing silently at runtime
on a Heltec LoRa V3 / ESP32-S3 SPI DMA path.

Covered (both CCSDS and SNLP tiers):
  PacketH_t, PacketA_t, PacketB_t, TunnelData_t,
  PacketAck_t, PacketC_t, PacketD_t, HeartbeatPacket_t

Existing SIZE_PACKET_X mismatch asserts are preserved unchanged.
